name: Sachertorte
origin: Created in 1832 by Franz Sacher, a 16-year-old apprentice cook, for Prince Wenzel von Metternich in Vienna; the subject of a decades-long legal dispute between the Hotel Sacher and Demel's bakery over the right to call their version 'Original'.

ingredients.note: melted dark chocolate at 100% of flour mass, reconstituted from two real registry substances rather than a single forward-referenced 'dark chocolate' id: cocoa butter (packages/data/substances/cocoa-butter.json, ~99.5% fat) plus cocoa powder (below) recombine, at roughly 46:54 by mass, to unsweetened baking chocolate's real ~53% overall fat content — the same pressing relationship cocoa-butter.json's own notes describe between the two files
residual fat fraction of the cocoa-powder share (54.2% of the 100%-of-flour chocolate charge) of the same reconstituted chocolate

process.name: cream butter, sugar and yolks
process.description: beat butter with half the sugar and the egg yolks until pale, then beat in the melted chocolate

process.name: whip whites
process.description: whip the egg whites with the remaining sugar to a stable meringue

process.name: fold together
process.description: fold the meringue and the sifted flour alternately into the chocolate-butter base

notes: Egg mass around 1.8x flour, with dark chocolate near 1x flour mass, is representative of the Hotel Sacher's own published proportions for this cake. Rather than a single 'dark chocolate' line with no registry backing, the chocolate is reconstituted from cocoa-butter and cocoa-powder, both real substances in packages/data/substances, in the ratio that reproduces baking chocolate's real ~53% overall fat content — fully ledger-ready, unlike a forward-referenced substance id. The apricot-jam glaze under the chocolate icing (Sachertorte's other defining feature) is a separately-prepared finishing component applied after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
